en: I wore my scarf ___ it was cold.
“Because” gives the reason: it was cold.
Ali likes apples, ___ he does not like pears.
“But” joins two ideas that are different.
It was raining, ___ we stayed inside.
“So” tells us what happened next because of the rain.
Would you like milk ___ hot chocolate?
“Or” gives a choice between two things.
I have a puppy ___ a kitten.
We go to the beach ___ the sun is out.
“When” tells us the time something happens.
The baby is tired, ___ she is going to sleep.
“So” shows what happens because she is tired.
Sam was sad ___ he lost his ball.
“Because” gives the reason Sam was sad.
The snowman melted ___ the sun came out.
“When” tells us the time the snowman melted.
Which word joins two ideas to give a reason?

example.q_en: I wore my scarf ___ it was cold.
example.why_en: “Because” gives the reason: it was cold.

en.title: Joining words
en.teach: Joining words link two ideas: and, but, because, so, or, when. I wore my coat because it was cold.
